conclusion: Control of the project management services transfers over time: each On-site Day is accepted when the customer signs the timesheet for that day (CON-X03-T1), and the customer receives and consumes the benefit of each day's work as it is performed (paragraph 35(a)), so revenue is recognised for each On-site Day on its customer-signed timesheet. Clause 6.1 (CON-X03-T3) requires a credit of $350.00 for each half day the project manager is absent, which reduces the price; the invoice is issued after the sixth On-site Day and is due within 10 days (CON-X03-T2).

reasoning_chain.text: Clause 4.1 (CON-X03-T1): each On-site Day is accepted when the customer signs the timesheet for that day.
Clause 6.1 (CON-X03-T3): if the project manager is absent for part of an On-site Day, the Supplier will credit $350.00 for each half day of absence.
Clause 5.1 (CON-X03-T2): the Supplier will issue a tax invoice after the sixth On-site Day, payable within 10 days.
Revenue is recognised when (or as) the customer obtains control of the promised good or service (AASB 15 para 31).
Control transfers over time if the customer simultaneously receives and consumes the benefits provided by the entity's performance as the entity performs (AASB 15 para 35(a)).

The customer accepts the services day by day on the signed timesheet, receiving and consuming the benefit of each On-site Day as it is performed, so paragraph 35(a) is met and control transfers over time.
Revenue is recognised for each On-site Day on the customer-signed timesheet, not on the invoice after the sixth day; the clause 6.1 absence credit reduces the price for the days concerned.

counter_argument: A timesheet left unsigned for an On-site Day, or a term making acceptance of all six days a condition of payment, would defer recognition for the days concerned.
